missionPremise: The dispatch's premise is that `src/jobs/parcel-record-fill.mjs` writes CAD `absent-verified` when its join finds nothing, and that on Williamson the P-266 dry run would stamp it on all 282,569 parcels. Verified at source in this clone, and the finding is LARGER than the dispatch's framing in one respect and SMALLER in another, both stated here rather than smoothed over: (a) LARGER: the emitter is the vendored engine (src/lib/parcel-record-engine/ingest-existing.js applyCadJoinMiss -> cadJoinMissVerified), reached from ingestCadOntoRecords; the job's OWN header (reportNullAtSourceMapping) still documents the opposite invariant ('every row's cell stays unaccounted on a join miss'), which was true at engine a38cbb2 and was not updated when commit 739731f re-vendored engine dfdf6fd on 2026-09-05 under the operator ruling _decisions/2026-09-05_cad_join_miss_becomes_absent_verified.md. So the file has documented the correct behavior for twelve days while the code it calls did the opposite, and P-268 exists only because of that divergence. (b) SMALLER: the engine copy is PINNED (ENGINE_PIN.json, engineSha 2cc2057, 'do not edit these .js files by hand', guarded by test/engine-pin-divergence.test.mjs), so the honest fix in THIS repo is job-side, exactly the layering P-268 and every other job-level step in this file already uses. The 2026-09-05 ruling's own REVERSAL CRITERIA ('if a real, identified population of parcels exists ... whose miss means a key-format mismatch rather than a genuine absence -- this ruling does not apply to that population') is the clause P-325 and P-310 together invoke; P-325 makes the fail-closed side of it uniform, P-310 identifies the population.
completionPredicate: P-325 done means: a join miss leaves the cell `unaccounted`, the run records the unresolved population by county and by rail, a join that RESOLVES and finds no value still writes `absent-verified`, both directions are proven on fixtures at the dispatch's own scale, the call sites are enumerated including the ones that would survive a naive removal, and the whole repo test suite is as green as main. P-310 done means: a decision with counts -- the writer's join read from code AND rows, the apply's value-to-absent movement per rail, and a recommendation among (a) situs-address recovery, (b) crosswalk, (c) apply as measured -- delivered to the operator, with no apply run. A close may say closed for P-325 and closed-partial for P-310 only if the decision is filed with its counts.

p325Built.what: neutralizeCadJoinMissAbsences(records) returns every cell carrying the engine's join-miss signal (isCadJoinMissBasis -- the engine's own predicate, the same one P-268 keys on, never a copy) to plain {kind:'unaccounted'}, and returns a census {parcelsTouched, cellsUnresolved, byRail}. Wired into instantiateAndIngest AFTER completeJoinMissCompanionsOntoRecords and strictly BEFORE the D1 derivations; accumulated per page in fillCountyWide as joinMissUnresolved {countyFips, parcelsTouched, cellsUnresolved, byRail} and printed on the county-wide log line. deriveAcreageSqftOntoRecords additionally refuses to derive an absence from a join-miss basis, so a caller that gets the order wrong still fails closed.
p325Built.whyTheOrderAndWhyP268Stays: The sweep runs after P-268's companion completion so the whole cohort (13 engine scalars + 2 companions) is cleared in one pass; P-268 is kept, not deleted, because it is the run-time evidence that the cohort is swept whole and because deleting it would silently drop the only test coverage of the engine signal. The derivation guard exists because acreageSqft would otherwise carry basis source 'derived-acreage-acres' -- not the engine's join-miss signal -- and so would SURVIVE the sweep as a second fabricated absence. That is the call-site finding this lane adds.

p325CallSiteEnumeration._why: Dispatch: 'Enumerate the call sites before you claim the defect is closed. A default copied into its callers survives its own removal.'
p325CallSiteEnumeration.emitter: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/ingest-existing.js applyCadJoinMiss (13 stamps) -> cadJoinMissVerified. Sole caller: ingestCadOntoRecords (same file, line ~272). Engine is PINNED; not edited.
jobConsumersThatWouldSurviveANaiveRemova: completeJoinMissCompanionsOntoRecords (P-268): consumes the join-miss basis and WRITES two more absences (acreageMethod, landUseSource). Handled explicitly: the sweep runs after it and clears both, and the census counts them (15 rails, not 13).

deriveAcreageSqftOntoRecords: consumes an absent-verified acreageAcres and WRITES a second absence with a DIFFERENT basis (source 'derived-acreage-acres'), which isCadJoinMissBasis does not match. Handled twice: the sweep runs before it, and the function itself now refuses a join-miss basis. This is the one that a naive 'sweep the join-miss cells' fix would have missed, and it is why the census reports 15 rails while the engine stamps 13.
p325CallSiteEnumeration.otherWritersOfTheSameConvention: src/jobs/parcel-owner.mjs (owner rail): a join miss leaves the cell UNTOUCHED, and its header says so explicitly -- 'This is a join miss, not a tested absence ... both leave a join miss unaccounted rather than fabricating an absent-verified. This job matches that established convention.' That comment also asserts the ENGINE behaves this way, which was false from 739731f until this branch. The two writers now agree, and the comment is true of both.
bypasses: A hand INSERT/UPDATE on parcel_record_cell (the module header already names this as the bypass for its ownership guards). P-325 cannot see it and states so.
Any future writer that reaches the same 13 rails with its own absence vocabulary. The guard is per-job; there is no engine-side refusal, and the engine-side re-scope is carried as OPEN in the close.
UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL itself: it refuses to downgrade a non-unaccounted cell to unaccounted, so the sweep CANNOT clear a join-miss absence already stored. Measured residue is in CP2.

programLawDeclaration._rule: OPS-24 dispatch program context item 7: any write that puts an unaccounted cell on a slated rail turns that whole county's ledger values back to the bake, and 'a lane whose writer can do that states it in CP1 and does not apply before P-297.'
programLawDeclaration.declaration: THIS WRITER CAN DO THAT, and this lane runs NO APPLY. Under P-325 a join-miss cell is left `unaccounted` where the old writer would have published a fabricated `absent-verified`. That is the intended direction -- the bake over a lie -- and it is a behavior change a reader must not have to infer. Nothing is applied by this lane: the fix is fixtures, tests and a PR.
programLawDeclaration.secondOrder: For an already-stored cell the direction is the opposite and safer: UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL refuses to downgrade a non-unaccounted cell to unaccounted, so a cell that currently holds a real VALUE survives a P-325 apply untouched, where the pre-P-325 apply would have overwritten it with a false absence. P-325 strictly shrinks the blast radius of this writer on an already-populated county.

p310PreRegistration._rule: Dispatch: 'pre-register what result would prove your join reading wrong, and state it before you measure.' Written before the lease was taken and before any store read.
p310PreRegistration.codeReadSoFar: loadLandingAndCad (src/jobs/parcel-record-fill.mjs:1440-1458) builds cadByProp for a SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS county (Hays 48209, Williamson 48491) ENTIRELY from loadAccountCrosswalk, whose SQL joins txgio_parcel.geo_id = cad_property.property_number (uniqueness-gated) and whose JS corroborator REFUSES a bind unless quickRefIdNumericStem(quick_ref_id) === node_prop_id. The R->numeric situs-address crosswalk (WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL / loadWilliamsonCrosswalk) is called with `[...cadByProp.keys()]`, so it can only FILL a key the geo_id crosswalk already bound, and the file's own comment states that for Williamson 'cadByProp starts empty ... so this is a no-op there until a future re-ingest makes the geo_id bind live'. If that holds, every Williamson node is a join miss, the numeric roll slice is unreachable through the writer, and the pre-P-325 writer stamps 13 (or 15) absences per parcel.
p310PreRegistration.prediction: The writer's Williamson join resolves ZERO nodes: cadByProp is empty for 48491, because txgio_parcel.geo_id carries no usable value on the numeric node population (or cad_property.property_number does not carry the matching identifier), and the R-keyed roll is never consulted for a numeric node.
p310PreRegistration.falsifier_thatWouldProveMeWrong: Any ONE of these, measured in the store: (F-A) the ACCOUNT_CROSSWALK_ROWS_SQL bind count for 48491 is materially non-zero (say > 5% of nodes) -- i.e. geo_id is populated on the node population AND property_number matches it uniquely; (F-B) landing_parcel_jurisdiction's 48491 prop_id population is R-PREFIXED rather than numeric, which would make the writer's node population the R-roll and my 'numeric nodes vs R roll' framing wrong; (F-C) cad_property for 48491 holds NO R-prefixed rows at all (so the roll is not R-keyed); (F-D) parcel_record for 48491 already holds cad_property-sourced VALUES on the join-miss rails in large numbers, which would mean some earlier path resolved these nodes and the join is not the whole story.
p310PreRegistration.interrogationIfItAgreesTooNeatly: The code comment already asserts 'cadByProp starts empty', so a row read that merely confirms it is a confirmation of a prior claim, not an independent one. I will therefore measure the two halves SEPARATELY and in this order: (1) the node keyspace and its cardinality, (2) txgio_parcel.geo_id's null/blank/format distribution on that same population, (3) cad_property's own key formats and property_number population, (4) the bind count of the crosswalk query itself, (5) the per-rail stored cell census. If (2) and (3) both look healthy while (4) is zero, the defect is in the JOIN, not in the data, and the recommendation is not about the keyspace at all.
p310PreRegistration.perRailValueToAbsent_measuredHow: For each of the 15 join-miss rails: count parcel_record_cell rows for 48491 by kind, so the value-to-absent movement the pre-P-325 apply would have caused is the count of cells currently holding a real value on that rail (the apply overwrites the whole record, so 'currently unaccounted' does not protect a cell). Reported per rail, never as a total.
